ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Embedding a hotpot exercise into a lesson
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi James, Please note that the only stage where you can indeed import questions (from various formats) into the Lesson is immediately after creating a new lesson. You cannot import questions into a Lesson which already contains questions. You do not import "a hot potatoes question" into the Lesson, you import a whole Hot Potatoes exercise, consisting of usually more than one question. When you create a HP exercise on your computer, using the HP software, you save it under 2 different types of files: a) the original HP format, which is e.g. for the JQuiz exercises a *.jqz file and b) an HTML file. The HP original files are in fact XML files, there is nothing more to do about them. I have just tested importing HP files into a new Lesson on my moodle 1.9.4 installation. I can report success with the following HP types: JQuiz (OK), JMatch (not quite right). Please note that you will lose all image & audio links in the import process. This import process will not really answer your query to " insert a hot potatoes exercise into the middle of a lesson". There are other ways to do it, but you'll have to accept the fact that the HP grades will not be transmitted to the gradebook. Hope that helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Embedding a hotpot exercise into a lesson
ResponsesInList.Text: James, here we go... Create a HP exercise on your local computer. Export as HTML Upload the HTML HP exercise to your moodle course files In moodle, create a lesson (or use an already created lesson) create a Branch Table (funny terminology ) on the Branch Table edit page, in the Page contents HTML editor, click on the Toggle HTML source button in the HTML source, write this code: <iframe height="400" width="100%" src=" http:/moodle/file.php/9/choices.htm "></iframe> of course replace the URL in red with the actual URL address of your HP exercise in your course files you may have to customize the height and width parameters according to your HP exercise "size"; experiment save See result on attached screenshot. Your HP exercise is "embedded" inside your Lesson page. Please note that the scores obtained by the students in that HP embedded exercise will not be passed on to either the HP activity nor the Lesson activity and therefore will not be passed on to the gradebook. Hope this will help, Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Regular Expression Help Needed
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ben, The Regular Expression option for short answer questions is powerful but very tricky to manage. First let's start with one expression you got wrong because it does not work as expected: Answer 2: --(Stephanie|scholar|she|problem|solution|her) Feedback 2: Sorry, you left out at least one noun or didn't capitalize the proper noun. How one would expect it to work: If any of those words is missing from the student's response, then the response is wrong. How it actually works: If none of those words is present, then the response is wrong. But if any of those words is present, then this is OK, continue analysis. This is really a bug in the way the regular expressions option works in the Lesson module, but I'm afraid it will stay as is for the moment. Please see my note about the Quiz option below. The only way to test whether obligatory words are present in the student's response is e.g. as follows: --Stephanie.*scholar.*problem.*solution.* The .* regular expression means "any character repeated any number of times including none". This tests not only the presence of those four words (nouns) in the student's response, but also their respective order in the response. Which explains that you have te be careful with the wording of your feedback message upon detecting an error. There is another hitch. It is possible to type a list of "unwanted" words, which will be displayed with an "incorrect" CSS style, by starting an expression with ++ (as you tried out). Unfortunately there is a bug in current versions of Lesson in Moodle which I reported (with a fix) as MDL-12860 (You can vote for it). Even when this bug is fixed you still need to provide an .incorrect{} rule in your current Moodle theme, because it does not exist in standard distributed themes. Anyway, here is what I suggest for your analysis: Short Answer - Use Regular Expressions Answer 1: Stephanie S scholar SC she S problem DO solution S her OP Response 1: Excellent work. This is a tricky sentence because it contains three clauses. You correctly identified all six nouns / pronouns. Stephanie (S) scholar (SC) she (S) problem (DO) solution (S) her (OP) Jump 1: Next page Answer 2: ++( a |is|and|as|pondered|the|suddenly|occurred|to) Response 2: Sorry, not correct. You probably included a word from the original sentence that isn't a noun or a pronoun. Jump 2: This page Answer 3: stephanie.* Response 3: Sorry, you didn't capitalize the proper noun. Jump 3: This page Answer 4: --Stephanie.*scholar.*problem.*solution.* Response 4: Sorry, you either missed or wrongly placed at least one noun. Jump 4: This page Answer 5: --.*she.*her.* Response 5: Sorry, you either left out or wrongly placed at least one pronoun. Jump 5: This page Answer 6: --.* S .* S .* S .* Response 6: There are 3 subjects in this sentence (S)! Jump 6: This page Answer 7: --.*DO.* Response 7: Sorry you left out one direct object (DO). Jump 7: This page Answer 8: --.*SC.* Response 8: Sorry you left out one subject complement (SC). Jump 8: This page Answer 9: --.*OP.* Response 9: Sorry, you left out an object of preposition (OP). Jump 9: This page Answer 10: .* Response 10: Try again. Jump 10: This page You can see it in action on my moodle test site here . Log in as moodler, password moodler. NOTE.- For a much better implementation of the regular expression answer analysis, you should use my regexp plugin for the Quiz module. This is still a 3rd party plugin, not part of the regular Moodle distribution, but if you plan to create lots of questions of this type then that plugin is a must. All the best, Joseph PS.- I see you are working in a "Center for Talented Youth". With bright students, you might even propose that the students themselves use the regexp plugin to create their own questions.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Regular Expression Help Needed
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ben, Some answers to your questions... 1- Applying the patch is dead easy. In your moodle installation, locate and open with a text editor file moodle/mod/lesson/action/continue.php. Around line 184, in the context below replace the line in red with the line in blue: break; // quit answer analysis immediately after a match has been found } } $studentanswer = s($useranswer); $studentanswer = $useranswer; break; case LESSON_TRUEFALSE : Note that if you want the 'extra wrong words' to appear in the feedback you'll have to add this CSS declaration: .incorrect {color:red!important;} (or something similar) to the end of one of your current theme's CSS files. 2- No, you can't author REGEXP questions as Quiz questions and import them to the Lesson module because they are totally different implementations. 3- Yes you can override roles to allow students to create their own questions in the Lesson module, maybe in a special moodle course set up for this purpose. Yes you can allow students to create their own questions in the Quiz questions bank. This is especially easy in Moodle 1.9. See the documentation . 4- There are a number of advantages to using the REGEXP question plugin in the Quiz module rather than the short answer, regular expressions option question type in the Lesson module: a- the teacher can view all the alternate acceptable answers b- students can have a Hint option c- all the students' responses are logged (saved) and can be reviewed individually by the teacher, which provides invaluable data on a) learning strategies b) is useful to improve the error analysis and provide relevant feedback. If you seriously envisage creating (or having the students) create a number of regular expressions questions, I would advise doing it in the Quiz module, not the Lesson module. You can test it on my test site (e-mail me for teacher access if you want). All the best, Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Flash Cards - I must be dense.
ResponsesInList.Text: Art, think of a deck of cards, on each card there's a question on one side and the answer on the other. Shuffle them and then deal them one at a time to your student. The student answers the question and can then turns over the card. Keep dealing single cards until the student has answered x questions, the deck is exhausted, the teacher's exhausted, the student's exhausted or the bell goes That's flash cards. In the lesson module you can also put as little or as much info with the question as you wish. HTH

ResponsesInList.Title: What is a Lesson, what is a Quiz and why can't I do it all?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Dane, Excellent post. I think one of the issues with Lesson is the purpose of a Lesson or that it's mission needs to be tightened. My sense is that due to popular demand, many things were added to Lesson at a time when Moodle was not as robust. I also believe that Lesson is used in many sites for different purposes, which at times means cross purposes. To sort the cross purposes (for example, I want to see Question titles on left along with Branch table titles, or I want to see some but not all page titles on the left), means changing settings and adding more variables to the module, or dividing the module up into similiar but different ones. Lesson can present pages in a adaptive manner. I suspect this is why the first standard module to have a conditional dependency built in was Lesson. In Version 2, when conditional dependency starts to become a Moodle feature in many/all standard modules, we may start to see a change in Lesson. Lessons may become shorter and perhaps more numerous with Moodle conditional dependency. First conditional dependency of modules and resources within a course, will probably build demand for site dependencies of the nested if, then type conditions. Now we are really talking about adaptive (and complex) learning. I think one of the next logical development steps in Lesson is to be able to export and import any Lesson page(s). First to be able to import specific pages into another lesson, then to be able to import specific pages into other modules and import pages from other modules into Lesson. Just one example concerns Lesson being able to have access to the Question Bank. Exciting stuff, in short Lesson has a lot of different possible looks. Perhaps Lesson needs to be broken up into more specific modules. Right now, there is nothing else like a Lesson :} Best Chris

ResponsesInList.Text: I get the idea that there is no database for a student's answers. Sort of a bucket for a student to record number of correct answers, another for possible answers. Same thing for each question. It records how many students selected an answer but not which students. Edit: ((( I ferreted this out because I wanted to see the wrong answers my students were giving before they figured out the right ones. My questions are primarily short-answer format with 5 tries allowed before students are sent ahead. With this, you can see every response given by every student every time they attempted a lesson. I didn't think I saw this info in the individual student report Ben explained above, which is much more convenient if it suffices. ))) Actually you can get that info. It is in the useranswer field of the mdl_lesson_attempts table. But to make any sense of it, you've got to cobble together info from a few other tables. If you want to see the answers a particular student gave, you have to know the numeric id given to each student (mdl_user). Then you need to know the ids corresponding to the page/questions (mdl_lesson_pages) and the lesson to which pages belong (mdl_lesson). If you just want to look at what students have entered, and the answers to the different questions of the lesson are pretty easy to tell apart, you can get an idea from glancing over just the mdl_lesson_attempts table. I export the info from these tables from phpmyadmin (For each table, click the Export tab at the top, choose Excel, make sure labels will be in top line, and save) and then play with them in a big spreadsheet so I don't have to worry about messing up something in the real database inadvertently. cheers, Kristina

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Stephen, The next lesson's setting can use dependency. The next lesson isn't available to the student unless a grade of X is achieved. I haven't used Dependent On but here's the short statement. This setting allows this current lesson to be dependent upon a students performance in another lesson that is in the same course. If the performance requirement(s) is not met, then the student will not be able to access this lesson. Conditions for the dependency include: Time Spent: the student must spend this set amount of time in the required lesson. Completed: the student must complete the required lesson. ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Stephen, More dust for you to consider. I really don't understand the customer's need for a password (except the customer is always right). What is their real goal? Frankly, what they have outlined could allow the potential for an otherwise failing students to get the password and proceed on the buddy system. The purpose of dependency is to prevent a student from advancing to the next lesson. Students who do not meet the bar, receive a notice when they attempt to get into the next lesson that tells them why they can not enter. Chain linking lessons together with dependency keeps someone from skipping any lessons. One of the ways to beat this system is for students to share logins. Smart student does the lesson for their buddy. There is some contributed code out there which will ask a random question from a list the student has answered before, which sort of helps. Your customer will have to consider some form of Activity locking (a contributed code), to block other activities (including Lesson) from sight conditionally. Here is a work around that sort of meets your described objective (no code involved). Create a one page lesson, make it a question page, put the password in it, give credit for the answer "I will remember this password". Make this lesson dependent upon a previous lesson, you set the conditions. Now make the third lesson that requires a password both dependent upon the lesson with the password and that the student must have the password. Double security but I am sure it does anything more for the overall security. Best Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Can someone explain scoring on multianswer questions?
ResponsesInList.Text: My first try at creating a lesson and I'm having trouble understanding how the 'score' is determined for multianswer multiple choice questions. If I have 2 right answers (both have a score of 1) and 2 wrong answers and the student chooses one of the right answers, it will say "Your score is 1 (out of 1). " If the student chooses both right answers, it will say "Your score is 1 (out of 1). " If the student chooses 1 right and 1 wrong it will say "Your score is 1 (out of 1). " If the student chooses 1 right and 2 wrong it will say "Your score is 0 (out of 1). "

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can someone explain scoring on multianswer questions?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Lynn, I have not played around with the scoring functions of multianswer type in a while. I just responded to Tom's post which sort of related. Thanks for your post, I will see if I can reword MoodleDocs about Lesson pages to make a better explanation. In a multianswer question type, the student either answers the entire question correctly, or does not. There is no partial credit. That is the way it works . And all the correct answers should have the same jump, same score and same response. And all the wrong answers should have the same jump, same score and same response. And that is the way that works . So a student who only picks 1 of 2 correct answers, misses the question. The score (remember it is identical for every wrong answer) the teacher has selected for a wrong answer is recorded. When the student picks both the correct answers, they receive credit. When the student picks both the correct answers and one of the wrong answers, they missed the question. I turned on custom scoring, displayed score, allowed review and 5 attempts in demo.moodle.org. As teacher I gave 2 points for the correct answer and -1 for a wrong answer. The student only got 2 points when they selected just the two correct answers. Any other combination, they received -1 . Hope this helps. Best Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: What is difference between a Lesson and Quiz?
ResponsesInList.Text: What is the difference? Lesson and Quiz both ask questions, have similar type questions that can be put in an order or appear in random order, the answers can be randomize, scored, have feedback fields and the each can be part of Grades . Both Lesson and Quiz have a page type for inserting information that is not scored. Both have the HTML editor tool to use in questions and answers. Lesson is all about giving a student choices on every lesson page which lead them to a place the teacher has pre-determined. Lesson has jumps associated with its question answers . Lesson has some special navigation pages. Lesson has choice buttons associated with its non scored pages . Quiz is all about finding out what a student knows and sharing that with them and with the teacher. It has a robust set of question types , can share questions with other quizzes with more options in scoring , regrading , and has multiple kinds of reports about student performance in the quiz or about the questions.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Adding static pages between questions in a lession
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Prem There are two possibilities to achieve what you want. Option 1- Add a Question page from the tabs, select Multiple choice enter the text of your "static page" in the Page contents box do not enter any text in any question or response box leave Jump1 set to "next page" Click the save page button Option 2- Add a Branch table enter the text of your "static page" in the Page contents box in the Description 1 box, enter "Continue" or "Next Page" (or any similar message which will be displayed on a button at the bottom of your static page). leave Jump1 set to "next page" click the Add a Branch table button Joseph PS.- Chris, as maintainer of the Lesson documentation, would you please add these instructions in the documentation? It's a pity though that there is no "Description" tab in the Edit Question Page tabs list, it would make things much easier!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Trying to get Moodle to do exactly what I'm looking for...
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Adam, Bill and Mary giving good advice, I do think a Lesson activity is what you want. Bill is a really brave person working with clusters in Lesson. This is really a question for the Lesson Forum, however. Here is some short hand clues that elaborate a bit on what has already been presented in this thread. B1, B2 etc are branch tables. The teacher does not enter any jumps, so Lesson automatically puts a continue button for the student to select. Q1, Q2 ect are questions and the teacher sets the jumps. Here is a lesson in logical order, there are 3 learning points for the student. B1, B2, B3, B4, Q1,B5, B6, B7, Q2,B8, B9, Q3. The student starts with B1 and presses the continue button to go to B2 . Ditto with B3 and B4. The continue button on B4 will take them to Q1. Say it is a multiple choice question. The correct answer takes them to B5. A wrong answer gives them a custom response and send them back to B1 for review. This cycle repeats itself. The student can not advance past Q1 unless they pick the correct answer. (Yes you can set a limit to the number of attempts so the student doesn't get into an endless loop). It is possible to add more questions at the end. These will be our review questions. For the sake of example, our review starts with B10 and Q4 and the logical order could be: ..Q3, B10, Q4, B11, B12, B13, B14, Q5, B15, B16, B17. B10 could be an introduction to our close. All students go to Q4. If they answer it correctly, the jump to Q5. If they miss they jump to B11 which continues to B13. These two pages present the information in a completely different manner. B14 might give them a choice to jump back to Q4, B11 or Q5. Or you could make B10 a classic branch table, where you could allow the student to pick the next question type. B14 would have similar jumps as mentioned before. Things are very structured. Now you could get tricky and use the dependency settings in lesson. You could set one lesson up to become an exam gatekeeper. For example you have L1, L2...L9, L10. Say you set up L3 as a 20 question Lesson. Students can not enter L4 until they score 80% on L3. This forces them to go back and retake the earlier lessons to pass L3. You may notice that I used Branch tables to present most of the content, rather than question pages. That is our style, we use question pages like a pop quiz. Certainly your whole Lesson could be made of question pages. Many Moodlers do exactly that but they are in a different environment. All question pages sort of makes dependency settings more problematic for what we do. That should get your going. I have to toddle off to home and bed. It has been a long day. Hope this helps Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: General 'How-To' help regarding Lesson Hiding/Locking
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Greg, My answer was Yes (here is why) and then you used the word "seen". For that you have to go to a contributed module (aka non standard). Some flavor of Activity Locking. Check the forum on Conditional Activities . Version 2 is rumored to have conditional stuff as standard. In general you can link one lesson to another based upon a score. Students can see but are told they can not enter until the get a specific score (in your case) on the previous lesson (which is specifically mentioned). Daisy chain the lesson together, then a student must take 1 before 2, and 2 before 3 and so on. A student takes 1 but tries 5 they will be told to take 4 but they didn't take it and will have to work back down the chain until they get in. That is your goal, asynchronous education without a specific class taking a course in a fixed period. Set up the course with topics, not weeks. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Regular Expression NOT case insensitive
ResponsesInList.Text:
Ben, The problem is not with case sensitive or not but with the formulation of your regular expression for the correct answer. Try this: Answer 1: 
```text
During warmups(,|) before the game started/i
```
 or this: 
```text
During warmups(,)? before the game started/i
```
 There is no reason to include an optional comma at the end of the expected correct answer. Please be careful with the blank spaces too. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grades for all Lessons in a course?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Maram, You should be able to click on "Grades", in the "Administration Section" of your course, then up the top you will see two tabs, "View Grades", and "Set Preferences". Click on "Set Preferences;" then click on "Use Advanced Features." Once you do this you will see more tabs. " Set Categories ," "Set Weights ," " Set Grade Letters ," and " Grade Exceptions." You will need to click on "Set Categories." Then create a category named "Lessons." After that you will be able to set all of your lessons to that category. When you "View Grades" again you will see the lessons with their score next to the total available for lessons, A further refinement you might make is to weight your lessons, and/ or set other categories such as Quizzes, or Tests etc. I hope this helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moving Lesson to another course
ResponsesInList.Text: Step-by-step. On your Moodle site front page you have Lesson01 and Lesson02. On your Moodle site you have Courses A, B, C, ... You want to backup Lessons01 and 02 and restore them to e.g. Course A. On your Moodle site front page, go to Site Administration, Front page, Front page backup and click. On the Course backup: page, only select Include:Lessons Lessons01 and Lesson 02 (no User Data) Next page message says: "Backup Details: Include Lessons without user data Lesson 01 Lesson 02". Click Continue. Next page message (bottom) says "Backup completed successfully". Click Continue. Next page ► Administration ► Front Page ► Front Page restore. In the list of saved backups (Name Size Modified Action) spot the recently saved file (something like File backup-moodle19dev-20080318-1528.zip 2.2KB 18 Mar 2008, 03:32 PM. Click on the name of the zip file and save to disk on your local computer (remember where you save it for further use). On your Moodle site, go to Course A. Go to Administration/Restore. On the ► CF101 ► Files ► backupdata page, click the Upload a File button. Navigate to the place where you just saved the zipped file e.g. backup-moodle19dev-20080318-1528.zip and upload this file to the backupdata folder of Course A. When this is done, in the Action column click on the Restore link in the row corresponding to e.g. the backup-moodle19dev-20080318-1528.zip file. Top message: "You are about to start the restore process for:" etc. Do you want to continue? Click Yes. Next page: ► Course restore ► backup-moodle19dev-20080318-1528.zip. Click Continue. Top message: Restore to: Select: Existing course, adding data to it and click Continue Next page: Choose a course : select Course A from the list of existing courses. Next page:Please note that this process can take a long time. Click the Restore this course now! button. Next message: Restore completed successfully. Click Continue. Et voila! in only 14 easy steps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: multi answer question problem
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Gunilla, Humm, this has to do with the nature of each specific question type. Lesson is looking for the correct answer. Take a close look at your multiple choice questions that work. All answers go to the next page. Students get to make one choice, all choices are correct because they go to the next page. I tried a short answer in demo.moodle.org. I left all answers blank. The continue button appeared because there was no answer for it to evaluate. Since you want the student to attempt an answer, you need to put a wildcard "*" in the first answer and double check that it is sending the student to the next page. I believe issue for a numeric and a multi answer question is that there is no way to accept all possible answers as correct. At the moment there is not a wild card you can put in the first answer of a numeric question (like I suggested for the short answer question) that will select all answers as being correct. My suggestion is to use the short answer as if it were a numeric and see how that works. In the case of a multi answer question, it is the logic in the question type itself. This is hard for me to explain. The student either gets the question completely right or get the question completely wrong in this type of Lesson question. This is not obvious to the teacher but is the way it works in the Lesson module. So if you set all the answers to this page, any and all answers would be wrong. If you set all answers to next page, then the student would have to select all the answers to get the question correct. I don't have a suggestion on how to work around this problem. I believe Quiz questions handle things differently. You can give credit for a wrong answer in multi answer question and you can use a wild card in a numeric question.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Object Reuse
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jon, You ask a very important question, and what you are trying to do makes a lot of sense. However I would use the term "learning object" with caution. In particular, I would not equate "learning object" to "Moodle activity or resource." A learning object is something more fine-grained than a Moodle activity. It is a small, self-contained chunk, typically 2 to 15 minutes in length, that can be reused in multiple contexts for multiple purposes. The learning objects vision is to have a repository of learning objects tagged with metadata that can be searched by course developers, who can build things like lessons by aggregating learning objects "on-the-fly." In the LMS world, I think the learning objects vision is most closely approximated by SCORM (I'm sure there will be other opinions on this!). Each learning object corresponds to a SCO, SCO's can be aggregated into a SCORM package, and the SCO's can be organized in different ways to produce complete courses or course units (SCORM 1.4 permits very flexible organization). Moodle activities , on the other hand, have an inherently monolithic design. They are self-contained and cannot share content. I do not believe you can use them for what you are trying to do, at least not in a "natural" way.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can you prevent Answers being randomised in Lessons?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Excellent question. In the past and in the current version, I will say " no". Moodle Lesson 1.8 module does not have the Quiz setting "Shuffle within questions". Thank you for the post, I changed MoodleDocs to answer this relatively common request. Hopefully, we will change it with 1.9. However, a developer will have to tell us if this feature is going to be available in the future. Currently the "new" Question Bank has a shuffle option property associated with individual questions (one multiple choice question's answers can be shuffled, while another multiple choice question's answers are randomized). In 1.8, only the Quiz module uses the Question Bank, but the plan is for any Moodle Module to be able to access this bank. Lesson in 1.8 does not use the Question Bank, and can only import questions that have been exported by Question Bank . ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Show/Hide Images in lesson page
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ali, I always have the dumb workarounds. You could do it the other way, make people who want to see the image take an action. For example, put an HTML link to the image on a Lesson page. Link text or maybe put an image icon that means something like "potentially distressing" as the link. Thus the picture would not blast someone at first. Another way is to put a branch page at the top with 2 student choices "show me all the pictures" or "I really don't want to see distressing pictures". Essentially create two independent branches that only start and end at the same pages. That would mean duplicating all your pages which is not easy to do in Lesson. In some versions of Moodle, I have been able to use an internal link in a lesson to another hidden activity (such as a lesson). This allowed me to use a lesson page as an index to other lesson activities . The link was in the content area, not in the jump. In this kind of work around you could duplicate the lesson with all pictures via copy and restore. Then I would go to the lesson "without distressing pictures" and simply delete the distressing pictures. ResponsesInList.Title: Delay if wrong answer is selected
ResponsesInList.Text: My Moodle 1.6.5 is working fine. My problem is with my students. Some want to learn and some don't. My system must be configured so the students can guess and eventually proceed through the course. I had one student view 250 pages in 90 minutes. I don't think he was even reading the questions. I am sure he was not reading any of the material. My wife is a Behaviorists. She asked if the program was capable of creating a 5 minute delay should the student select the incorrect answer at the end of a lesson. Could you imagine the positive impact if a student found that by answering correctly they could finish sooner. Are there any time constraints associated with the lesson module? Is there any work being done to added time constraints? Who or where would I put this suggestion to have it considered? Thanks ... Michael

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Delay if wrong answer is selected
ResponsesInList.Text: I call these user the speed clickers. I agree with your wife, make them pay in what they value - "time". I am not aware of any lesson delay for speed clicker. I have two basic suggestions. 1. We send them back in the logical order when they miss a question. "They need review if they missed that one" is the official policy. As the Behaviorist implies, the speed clickers want to zip through our branch and question pages. It doesn't take our adult trainees long to realize it takes less time to read the questions we scatter about than randomly guess the answers. You might need to be clever about this. Don't do every question the same way for wrong answers. When they miss "the answer", send them back to the "this page" some times, send them forward as if they got it correct, send them back 10 pages at other times. Insert a page in the logical order that is intentionally skipped but guesses will hit it. Speed clickers will figure out the back browser button to skip the review and answer the question correctly, so random really makes them pay attention because of the cost of being lazy or non-motivated. I have varied my standards from lesson to lesson (hey I am lazy too) just to keep them guessing about the pattern. Also remember, some of these students will not realize they just answered 500 questions and only needed to answer 50 questions. Just like they might not realize you sent them to a time out area for 5 minutes (boring is boring). So you may have to tell them what you are doing a couple of times early on in the lesson. Not only in the intro, but as feed back "Sorry you missed this question, please review this material". Can you find a reward that a student has to find? Puzzle pieces, build a magic phrase that allows them to draw a prize (a credit for a book report? an apple for the teacher?) . 2. Install Activity Locking in 1.6.5 or upgrade to 1.8 and use the built in Lesson dependency settings. One of the contingencies in either of these is time spent in another activity/lesson. Note: there maybe a problem with time because in the past it was not cumulative for all attempts of the lesson, just the current attempt or most recent attempt.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Text displayed above answer
ResponsesInList.Text: H Janneke, Maybe you had something different in mind for (a). I'm guessing that you have a text that will be the basis for several questions and you want that text to appear above those questions (but not associated with the first question). If so, you should put the text in a so-called Description question. It's one of the question types that you can choose from the in the pull-down menu when creating a new question. To achieve the effect you want in (b), I again use the Description question. But now it reads something like this: "The next five questions are based on a text. For the text, click here ." When students click the link, they get a popup window containing the text. They can keep the window open as they answer the next five questions, and they can resize the window or move it to an unused part of the screen. It achieves the same effect as what you are asking for. To get a popup window as described above is a little tricky. Create a Web page resource containing the text on the main course page and be sure to specify "New window." You typically don't want students to see the resource until they take the quiz, so put the resource in an unseen block (a block beyond the range of visible topics, say block 100 in a ten-topic course). Then copy the link to the resource into the link in the Description question.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Text displayed above answer
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Fred, "Unseen block" is a clever name for a design pattern described in this discussion . It is a topic block (not a side block). Suppose you have a course with 10 topic blocks. That means 10 topics are showing. If you go to Course settings and change 10 to 100, then 100 topics will show. You can put a resource in topic block 100. Then go back to Course settings and change the number of topic blocks back to 10. The stuff in block 100 will still be there, but it will be unseen! Whenever you (as teacher) want to add or change an unseen resource, you can temporarily change the number of topic blocks back to 100. Unseen is NOT the same as hidden.You will also see these resources in the resource indexes, as clever students will quickly discover, so it is not a perfect solution. The discussion I linked to above points to some tracker issues you might want to vote on.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Remember you can use branch pages (aka branch tables) without entering in any descriptions. This is similar to John's suggestion using question pages without answers. Branch pages are score neutral if this is or will be important to you. Without entering a description for the student to select, the continue button appears. You can set a jump in a question to go to a branch page ( or a question page). Place your external link in the content area of that page. On that page, I would put "Continue" in Description 1 or Answer 1 with the jump set to where ever you want. Essentially you are starting off using a question page as a classic branch page. You can also set up a branch page to act like a MC or T/F question page. This was useful in earlier versions of Moodle because of graphics. Or if you don't want to score or count as a question page. Sounds like you are already thinking along these lines but thought I would share anyway. Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grading
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Dave, The grading for lesson is rather tricky because it is possible that a user could answer any number of questions and skip any number due to branching and jumps. So, lesson looks at what the user actually attempted, scores those, and then scales it to the max grade setting. I believe this is for when Custom scoring is turned On. I think what you are looking for is when Custom Scoring is turned Off. With this setting turned Off, each question answered correctly equates to 1 and then the minimum number of questions attempted can be enforced. Hope this helps, cheers, Mark

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grading
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Dave, When custom scoring is turned Off, then correct/incorrect answers are determined by the jump. So if an answer jumps to this page or backwards in the navigational flow of the lesson, then it is incorrect. If the jump goes forward in the navigational flow of the lesson, then it is correct. I think this is what you are grappling with now. Cheers, Mark

The other potential problem you did not mention is that after being sent back then the students have to review all the pages. For example: If a students misses Q2 and is sent back to B3. The navigation order for B3 will still be in place. If you change the lesson setting to 1 attempt, then they will jump to B4, then go to B5 etc. In Alternative 1 this could be a lot of material. This falls under lesson planning. In Alternative 1, if an answer in Q3 indicates they missed the content of B2, then you might send them to another page which explains the concept differently. Then send them back to Q3 (which of course they answered) so they will automatically go to the next page (generally speaking). This can start to create lots of loops for a teacher to remember. Hope this assists you. Chris

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Eduardo, Basically, you want to be able to enroll a specific student in a specific activity, such as a Lesson, and you do not want other students to be able to see activities they are not enrolled in. I could not come up with a total solution. I did think about groups, passwords and roles. You could create a "group" for each student. You would have to issue passwords to the student. But the activity title can still can be seen by all students. You might look at Roles in 1.8. I don't have experience being creative with them. The Lesson in #8 was still hidden to my new user (not even grey). I don't know what I am doing in roles and there are lots of different permissions which can be set. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Roles? Re: activity for only one determined user
ResponsesInList.Text: I did try the roles idea on demo.moodle. As admin, I created a new user, hid the Lesson in Topic #8, then assigned my new student as Teacher (non-editing) to that Lesson. Then I loged in as new user. The Lesson in #8 was still hidden to my new user (not even grey). I don't know what I am doing in roles and there are lots of different permissions which can be set. As admin, create a copy of the Student role; let's call it "Privileged student". In the course context , override this role, giving permission to see hidden activities. Then using Administration -> Assign roles, assign selected users to this role. Such users will be able to see ALL hidden activities in this course, not only the hidden Lesson. The above depends too much on the Admin. We would like to minimize Admin involvement and let the teacher manage roles to the extent possible. But the Admin probably wants maintain control over which teachers can grant special privileges to students, as well as the courses in which they can do it. As a minimum, the admin must create a copy of the Student role (again, let's call it Privileged student) but don't override any of the permissions -- let the teacher do that. create a copy of the Teacher role, call it "Teacher who can manage roles" (TWCMR) In the Site Administration -> Users -> Permissions -> Define roles -> Manage roles tab, give TWCMR permission to (a) Override permissions for others and (b) Assign roles to others In the Site Administration -> Users -> Permissions -> Define roles -> Allow role overrides tab, allow TWCMR to override Privileged student In the Site Administration -> Users -> Permissions -> Define roles -> Allow role assignments tab, allow TWCMR to assign Privileged student To give selected teachers the role of TWCMR in selected courses, enter each course and in the Administration -> Assign roles -> Assign roles tab, assign the TWCMR role to the teacher. Now any user who is a TWCMR can override Privileged student and assign selected students to this role. Unfortunately, in any given context (e.g., course, block, or specific activity), the teacher can override the Privileged student role exactly once . If multiple roles are needed within the same context, the teacher must ask the admin to repeat the above procedure, creating Privileged student 2, Privileged student 3, etc. If you wanted to have all possible combinations of privileges for students in a forum, you would need 1,048,575 copies of Privileged student (see this discussion ).

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Chris! Thank you for working on this for me. There is a mistake in my post, however. The answers ARE displaying properly - the way the students type them in. I copied and pasted from another question on the last example by mistake and wasn't aware of it until I read your post. Forgive me. There are only 3 issues: The Jumps for an incorrect answer must be set to 'Next Page' in order for custom feedback on that incorrect answer to display. If the Jump is set to 'This Page', default feedback shows regardless of whether the 'Display Default Feedback' option is set to 'Yes' or 'No'. It always shows for an incorrect answer and custom feedback is ignored. Once the default feedback for an incorrect answer displays, there is an error there. The default display link of 'No, I want to go to the next question' doesn't go to the next question page, but instead links to the same page, just as the 'Yes, I'd like to try again' link does. So, there's no choice despite the options. Here's the scenario I want: I want to use the Lesson module as a type of Self-Practice & Review where the students attempt the questions and based on the feedback correct their errors. If the answer is correct, they move on. If the answer is wrong, they have the option of going back right then and correcting their error or they can move on to the next question. Afterall, sometimes, there is no amount of help that can lead to the correct answer. Sometimes, the only way to solve a problem is to just leave it and come again later. Being forced to answer a question to which you have no clue about solving can be disheartening, especially if you are in an endless loop. I have found this teaching philosophy/model SO effective in both academia and life: When students are allowed to make mistakes and immediately get feedback on WHY their answers are wrong, and then have the chance to immediately correct their own errors, they become better diagnosticians of their own errors. They make fewer errors because they are able to recognize their own mistake patterns. Thus, logic is applied, instead of mere data being transferred. As it is now, the students have 2 options: 1) is to make the mistakes, get the custom feedback that will help them, but have no way to immediately correct their errors.  2) Make the mistakes, get default feedback that does NOT help them, and be placed in an endless loop of trial and error without benefit of guidance. Neither of these are ideal.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 1.7 - Problems with learning paths and Custom feedback
ResponsesInList.Text: Posts crossing in the either. I am seeing cross eyed at this point in my day. I think what is getting in the way is the student review flow control settings. You don't need it and the custom response is more important to you. The custom response is displayed for every answer. When one does not exist, then the default response is displayed. The custom response does not seem to be displayed when the student review flow control button and student review allow settings are set to yes. The way to correct the endless loop is to set the maximum number of attempts at 2 or 3 in Lesson settings. Once a student reaches the limit, they automatically are moved along the logical order. Another option is to tell the student to use their back browser button to go back to the question again. If you are keeping score, the max attemps are counted when they submit an answer. So if it is set to 2, and a student misses the question 2 times but goes back to it with the back browser button, they will not get credit for a correct answer. They can however, visit it again and again and again. In recap, why you thought the only way to give a custom response to a wrong answer, was to send the student to the next page, was because of your student review settings in Lesson. Sending the student to the next page is one way to tell Lesson the student has made a correct answer. No student review is offered for a correct answer, thus the custom response kicked in. I think you should say no to both student review settings, and set max attempts to 2 or 3. Yeah, you want the students to do a self review, but those settings are not going to help you acheive your goal. You want an intelligent, teacher guided review, not a standard blah blah lazy teacher automatic response. And I only mean that in the kindest loving way to those who developed and those who use this wonderful feature . It is time to go home, my apologies and best to all - Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Start Branch, End Branch and Content pages?
ResponsesInList.Text: Just a suggestion, can we make the branch pages more robust?  Give them a name make over? John Isner got me thinking about "Branch Tables" again.  Some have heard this before, I believe that the first pages in the Lesson module were Question pages.   Then the concept of Branch was introduced and a Branch Table was added to MoodleLexicon.  Thus initially,  content was envisioned to be in questions and  Branch Tables had an area where the branch links could be described or prefaced. With all due respect to the MoodleElders, I would rename and redefine the whole branch table page concept in Lesson.   I would suggest a "Start Branch", "End Branch" and "Content" pages in a Lesson. The "new" Content page in the first release would look like a Branch Table.  It would be absolutely neutral in score.  However, Content pages will now appear inside a branch along with question pages. I would like to see both the new Content page and the "Start Branch" or the good old current "Branch Table" be more robust in the student selection area. It should be similar to "answers" in a multiple choice lesson question.  For example, click on the display HTML would allow a teacher to put in a picture, or create their own bar with text that is associated with a specific jump. Wonder what others think.  Why do I think the HTML suggestion is already on the drawing boards at HSU?   Thanks for all your efforts.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Start Branch, End Branch and Content pages?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Chris, Branch Tables have been overloaded, but I think the solution will have to come after the lesson to question bank conversion. There is a description question type (I think that is the name) and it could be used for a content page. I'm toying with the idea of removing End of Branches, Cluster, End of Cluster and the idea of jumps for each question answer and instead implement the idea of State Checkers . None of this is final, just brainstorming on ways to improve lesson and simplify editing. The switch to the question bank would be a good time to perform these changes so users will only have to learn a new system once and the module will only have to go through one migration process (meaning less opportunities for things to break). Cheers, Mark

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Start Branch, End Branch and Content pages?
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Mark for the link. That is a lot to grok for a mere bald mortal. I think you are on a couple of levels higher than me with the State Checker concept. You know my way of thinking: there are pages and navigational markers. I would rather call it a Page Bank . Lesson and quiz pages formats should be interchangable.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Start Branch, End Branch and Content pages?
ResponsesInList.Text: One of the states could be to randomize choices, another to randomize the navigational order and etc. Thus a lesson or lesson segment, could react just like a quiz. Yes, this is close to the goal, which is to make the lesson navigation system much more simple yet much more powerful/flexible at the same time. Currently, the navigation is controlled in each question, between a Branch and End of Branch, between a Cluster and End of Cluster or a mix of the above. I find it all confusing myself. I think it would be much more valuable to have the thought process go, "I need to send students to page X so I need to add a State Checker (or whatever it may be called)" rather than, "I need to send students to page X, should I add a branch table, a question, a cluster, etc etc". For the simple minded, Branches and clusters seemed to be special changes in the default navigational state in a lesson. I think this is important. There should be an overall default for how one navigates from one page to the next. EG: Correct answer goes to next page in the logical order, Wrong answer goes to same page. Then the lesson author adds in special markers to change the default navigation of the lesson. This allows for quicker lesson navigation building/editing because the editor does not have to enter every question, cluster, etc and change the navigation. Instead, just modify the default lesson navigation and the markers. Cheers, Mark

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Feedback trouble in 1.6
ResponsesInList.Text: Russ > Solved it myself! The culprit is the "display review button" setting (hereafter DRB). Good detective work, Russ. You did find the culprit. Here are my tests of the DRB setting (using Moodle 1.6.3 stable). Just using one ordinary MCQ question for this test. Here are the results of my tests with these lesson settings for Flow control. . Allow student review: No Display review button: Yes Maximum number of attempts: 3 Attempt 1: student makes incorrect choice Feedback displayed: " Unfortunately you cannot earn this one point, because your response was not correct. Would you like to keep guessing, just for the sheer joy of learning (but for no point credit)? " Available buttons: Yes, I'd like to try again No, I just want to go on to the next question Notice: You have 2 attempt(s) remaining NOTE.- If the teacher entered some feedback text in the Response field for that incorrect choice, it is not displayed to the student. Student clicks on the Yes, I'd like to try again button Attempt 2: student makes incorrect choice again Feedback displayed: "Not quite. Would you like to try again?" Available buttons: Yes, I'd like to try again No, I just want to go on to the next question Notice: You have 1 attempt(s) remaining Student clicks on the Yes, I'd like to try again button Attempt 3: student makes incorrect choice again Feedback displayed: "Not quite. Would you like to try again?" Available buttons: Yes, I'd like to try again No, I just want to go on to the next question (Maximum number of attempts reached - Moving to next page) Student clicks on the Yes, I'd like to try again button ... and is allowed to make another attempt; in fact is allowed to make as many attempts as he wants (but will not get the grade for this question ). Note.- If after Attempts 1 and 2 the student clicks on the No, I just want to go on to the next question button , the lesson does not move to the next question until he has reached the Maximum number of attempts allowed for this lesson, instead, the same question is displayed again. Conclusion: at the moment, the DRB setting a) overrides the display of negative feedback messages and b) does not take into account a maximum attempts number greater than 1. How can we get the DRB setting to work more logically? The easiest solution would be to warn the teachers that there is an incompability between DRB being set at Yes and Maximum number of attempts set at anything else than 1. Such a warning should be added to the online help for the DRB button, such as: Display Review Button This will display a button after an incorrectly answered question, allowing a student to re-attempt it. It is not compatible with essay questions, so leave this off if you are using essay questions. It is not compatible with Maximum number of attempts set at anything greater than 1. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Incorrect feedback behavior in the lesson module (Moodle 1.7)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jan, One sure way to get one's questions answered on the Moodle forums (as on any forum on the Web) is to give a maximum of details and concrete examples of one's problems (as pointed by Dr S Bhatia). Anyway, here is an example demonstrating how the MCQ-multiple choice answer question type works in Moodle 1.6 (and, I expect, in 1.7). Question Text: Which if these is an animal? Check one or more answers. Multiple Choice - Multianswer Answer 1: the cat Response 1: Correct. You have found all the animals. Jump 1: Next page Answer 2: the dog Response 2: Jump 2: Next page Answer 3: the tulip Response 3: Wrong. You have either not selected all of the animals or you have selected things which are not animals. Try again. Jump 3: This page Answer 4: the crocodile Response 4: Jump 4: Next page Answer 5: the computer Response 5: Jump 5: This page When the program analyses the student's answer, there are only 2 possibilities: all of the correct answers AND none of the incorrect ones have been selected the student's answer is marked as correct the feedback message ("Response") entered for the last expected correct answer in the sequence is displayed none of the correct answers OR only some of them have been selected OR all of the correct answers have been selected AND at least one of the incorrect answers has been selected the student's answer is marked as wrong the feedback message ("Response") entered for the last expected wrong answer in the sequence is displayed Because only one "wrong answer" Response message and only one "correct answer" Response message are used by the program, you should only enter one of each . If you enter only one of each, it does not matter whether you enter each message for the first or the last (or any other) correct/incorrect expected answer in the sequence. If you enter more than one Response message for each correct/incorrect case, then you encounter the problem mentioned by you and by Chris in his reply. Once you understand the system you realize that this is not a bug but "expected behavior" of this question type in the Lesson activity. Hope that helps, Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Incorrect feedback behavior in the lesson module (Moodle 1.7)
ResponsesInList.Text: Coda. My previous explanation of the workings of the MCQ, Multianswer question type in the Lesson module applies when - in the Lesson settings - Custom scoring: is set to No . If Custom scoring is set to Yes , things are a little different and get more complicated. Question Text: Which if these is an animal? Check one or more answers. Multiple Choice - Multianswer Answer 1: the cat Response 1: Correct. You have found all the animals. Jump 1: Next page Score:1 Answer 2: the dog Response 2: Jump 2: Next page Score:1 Answer 3: the tulip Response 3: Wrong. You have either not selected all of the animals or you have selected things which are not animals. Try again. Jump 3: This page Score:0 Answer 4: the crocodile Response 4: Jump 4: Next page Score:1 Answer 5: the computer Response 5: Jump 5: This page Score:0 Here you need to put the same , non-null score (Score > 0) into all of the correct answers . as in the example shown above. If you put a non-null Score for e.g. only the first correct answer, the student will get that Score but the "Wrong" feedback message will be displayed. If you put e.g. a score of 2 for correct answer #1 and a score of 3 for correct answer #2, if the student selects all the correct choices, he will get a grade of 2/3, etc. Hope that helps people understand the rather complicated workings of the Lessson module. Joseph

ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, Why should some students getting all the correct answers in a Lesson be stuck on a 44.44% total score. I have created two simple Lesson activities in my Moodle system (version 1.6.2+). They are 'simple' because there are no branches; both Lessons contain 8 questions, and when student get questions right they are taken to the next question in order, and if wrong, back to the question they got wrong. Students can do the Lessons as many times as they want. Now that some 80 students have done both these lessons, I notice that there is a problem with the scoring for Lesson 2: many students get 100%, however some students appear to have all the answers correct but are only getting 44.44%. All the questions are equally weighted (i.e. custom scoring has not been used). Lesson 1 contains only 'Multiple Choice - Multianswer' type questions, whereas the Lesson with the total score problem contains one 'Multiple Choice' and one Matching type question, and six 'Multiple Choice - Multianswer' type questions. Another difference difference between the two lessons is that one of the 'Multiple Choice - Multianswer' type questions in Lesson 2 has no incorrect answer. My intention was that students have to recognise that all 7 of the choices are correct, and so select all 7 of the choices in order to move to the next question. Could the lack of a wrong choice in this question be the cause? Or could there be another reason why some students getting all the questions right, are only getting 44.44%? And yes, students that are not getting all the questions right are getting correspondingly varied and expected scores.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Peter, Did you figure this out? Following up on Dr.'s question and point, if your Lesson setting "handling of retakes" is set to mean instead of max, then a student who re entered the lesson could never get 100%, if they missed a question on one of their earlier attempts. Oh yes, I have quickly glanced at the logs and assumed that the student took it once. Then realized that while I had correctly set the max attempts at any question to 1 and allowed retakes, my site default is to use the mean and....I forgot to switch it to max. My spreadsheet says 4/9 or 8/18 = 44.44% which might also have me looking at my lesson settings, perhaps max score combined with the mean might give a student a 44%. Then there is the back arrow on the browser that some of my students love to use. That is why I only give them one attempt on an important set of lesson questions. Our message: 'you don't pass the lesson, that is OK but you take the whole lesson over again, so give each question some careful thought the first time, thank you very much.' ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Peter, With custom scoring turned Off, if the user answers incorrectly and re-attempts the same question, then that user does not receive full credit for that question. In the lesson reports, I think it only shows their latest answer (which would be the correct one). One way to investigate this is to look at the logs for a particular student. Look to see if the user saw the same question more than once for a single attempt at the Lesson. Hope this helps, Mark

ResponsesInList.Title: Lessons In Sequence
ResponsesInList.Text: I have several courses broken up into 5-7 lessons. How can I ensure that the lessons are taken in sequence?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Lessons In Sequence
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Gerald, There are several ways. In 1.6 and onward, there is a way to make one lesson dependent upon another. This is set under lesson settings (updating lesson). There are 3 possible criterion time, completion and minimum score that can be used in combinations if desired. l See MoodleDocs access control There are some non standard modules for conditional activities : Activity locking or Score Lock. These are a little bit more complex, alter the Moodle database and allow most activities or sections to be dependent upon meeting certain conditions. Last I looked, these have not been updated for 1.7. Of course you can open and close lessons by dates to establish a sequence but that does not ensure a student has taken the lesson. Hope this helps

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questions about using the Lesson Module
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi James, Been down this road. You raised 3 points. I feel more comfortable with the last two. I think Lesson settings have most of the answers. You didn't say which version of Moodle so I will stick with 1.5.4 but this will generally be correct for 1.6 and 1.7. 1. See their results, see number of attempts. How about showing the students their running score. Others may want to make suggestions here, we don't use grades, just pass or fail. 2. Custom scoring . Go to Lesson settings and change the Max Grade from 0 (current setting from your description) to what ever you want. Alternative. Turn off custom scoring.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Questions about using the Lesson Module

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Trouble with Dependencies in Lessons
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, I can answer your question. Mainly because I ran into this as well and had to fix it. If it's not letting you go into "Lesson 2" even though you have completed "Lesson 1"...here's what you need to check. In the settings for "Lesson 2" where you have made it dependent on "Lesson 1", make sure that ONLY the box for "Completed" is checked. Make sure there is NOTHING in the time limit OR the % boxes. Save your changes. NOW, go to the settings for your "Lesson 1". There will be an area near the top where they ask you if the lesson will be a practice lesson. Make sure "No" is selected. If "Yes" is selected, and another lesson is dependent on you completing it, it won't work. When it's set as a practice lesson, Moodle doesn't consider it a real "Lesson". It will show up in the "Lessons" you can make others dependent on, but won't work. I hope this helps you. Let me know if it does. Sincerely, Leonda Metsker

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Import questions default blues
ResponsesInList.Text: In the Lesson module, in a question page, correct answers jump by default to Next page and incorrect answers jump to This page (i.e. student has to "try again"). When importing from a GIFT format file, this is exactly the mechanism which is used. If you want a student to be taken directly from one question to the next irrespective of their answer being correct or incorrect: in the Lesson Settings, set Maximum number of attempts: to 1. Please note, however, that a message "correct / incorrect" will still be displayed to the student upon answering each question. ResponsesInList.Title: Lesson development update
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Lesson Users, I wanted to give everyone an update in regards to current Lesson development.  The release of Lesson in Moodle 1.7 will not contain a lot of new features, but rather it will strengthen the code base to improve current features and future maintenance.  You can review the main changes in the Release Notes . The reason for limiting the new features is because the code needed a chance to mature.  Also, there is a planned overhaul detailed here: http://docs.moodle.org/en/Adding_question_types_to_lesson .  This overhaul will essentially require the module to be rewritten from the ground up.  So, to make this process easier, I'm limiting the number of new features and I'm improving the code base to make it easier to upgrade. These recent changes are rather large so please test the Lesson code in 1.7 so we can have a smooth release.  Moodle 1.7 has a planned release date of October 9th and I'm planning to spend time on my weekends to help stabilize the code. If you find bugs, please post them in the bug tracker.  I created a filter to view all open Lesson bugs to make it easier to help.  You can view the filter here: http://tracker.moodle.org/secure/IssueNavigator.jspa?mode=hide&requestId=10076 Cheers and happy Moodling, Mark

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Matching question problem in lesson
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jarsolav, Currently the matching question type is all or nothing. Why the final grade is not calculated f rom number of right and bad answers? The original Lesson counted answers as right or wrong based on the jump.  So forward progression in the Lesson was a correct answer and staying on the current page or moving backward in the Lesson was an incorrect answer.  So, this was an "all or nothing" system.  When custom scoring was introduced, the all or nothing method was still being used to allow for fewer discrepancies between the two scoring systems. Another reason is that you would have to assign a score for every correct match and every incorrect match.  This might become more complicated than what most users want.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: advice on jumps needed (fairly basic)
ResponsesInList.Text: Sorry for late answer.  I have been fighting alligators and crawling out of my own bottomless pits No custom scoring, OK.  You didn't tell us where the correct answer jump went.  However,  Lesson knows a student selected  a wrong answer because a student returns to the question or goes back in the logical order. That would suggest at least two options to me.  In lesson settings, allow retakes and set max attempts at 1 or 2 and show the student their score.  Add a choice for the student to retake the lesson or branch where it makes sence. In the first option, set the jump for a wrong answer to "this page".   When max attempts is set to 1, I don't think the student will actually see the page again.  The tricky part is if a correct answer sends the student to an eob, this will not happen for a wrong answer.  The student will be sent to the next page in the logical order.  So if random question was q2 they will go to eb1 but if first random question is q1 they will then go to q2.  Do you follow? My second option would be to add a branch page that basically is not seen by students unless they missed a question.  b1x, b1, q1, q2, eb1 b2x, b2, q3, q4, eb2, b3.   All students start the branch at b1. eb1 is set to jump to b2.  branch b1x description 1 says something and jump 1 is set to eb1 and do something similar for b2x.  Student who gets a question wrong will not see other random questions. Attached is one of my simple lessons I play with.  Branch A is set up so you can play with the two options above.  I did it in 1.6 but I believe it can be restored to 1.5.3  because it is so simple. Hope this helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: e+Learning vs. e-Learning
ResponsesInList.Text: Modelling of e-Learning Processes: an Approach Used in Plovdiv e-University George Totkov, Elena Somova, Mariana Sokolova Abstract: Most of the e-Learning systems don’t have means for modelling a learning process and in particular the structure and content of the virtual learning courses. In PeU learning environment virtual courses are designed by using directed graph with nodes of two types: informative (learning materials or groups of them – AND, OR, MORE etc.) and controlling (Join_Split, Repeat, Check_Point, etc. ). For the development and editing of courses in PeU, the authors use environment with visual programming elements.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: e+Learning vs. e-Learning
ResponsesInList.Text: BEST: New Lessons Module Logic Daniel Denev, Rositsa Doneva, George Totkov Abstract : Most of the known e -Learning environments do not have means for modelling the structure of the learning lessons, i.e. for representing the logical order in which the concepts are presented to the learners. In this direction, in the frame of the BEST project, a research for extending the functionality of the Moodle concept "Lesson module" is carried out. The paper presents the basic ideas and results of the research. The BEST project for development of a virtual learning environment focuses on didactic approach to e-learning . It is based on the following principles: learning is a goal-directed process (teachers have opportunity to define the lesson logics on the basis of its learning objectives and the possibility to monitor and measure the quality of the learning process); learning is embedded in a conceptual context , etc.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: e+Learning vs. e-Learning
ResponsesInList.Text: Content Management in e-Learning vs. Learning Design in e -Learning e-Learning has a well developed approach to the creation and sequencing of content-based, single learner, self-paced learning objects. However, there is little understanding of how to create sequences of learning activities wh ich involve groups of learners interacting within a structured set of collaborative environments, or how teachers can make these sequences easily re-usable (making national fund of re-usable learning sequences). Given that a key dimension of Bulgarian higher education is learning which arises from interacting with teachers and peers (rather than simply interacting with content), the lack of a mature approach to sequencing of multi-learner activities is a significant blind spot in e-Learning today. This is surprising given that "lesson planning" – the process of determining the sequence of activities to be followed by a lecturer and learners when studying a topic – is well understood in education, but is mainly absent from e -Learning. However, there is a growing body of work addressing this topic, based on the concept of "Learning Design". Learning Design provides a first glimpse at the ways of describing multilearner activity sequences and the tools required to support these. Learning Design has the potentia l to revolutionize e-Learning by capturing the "process" of education, rather than simply content management as it in Moodle. By describing sequences of collaborative learning processes in Bulgarian universities, Learning Design offers new pedagogical approaches to re -use in e-Learning. This article describes our joint Learning Design approach, a detailed example, and its implementation.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Student access to sequential lessons

ResponsesInList.Text: I think the short answer is no for Moodle out of the box.  Enrollment keys are for courses.   I am not the expert in this so there are probably addins and code work arounds. In 1.6 there is lesson dependency setting under access control.   There are 3 criterion:  time spent, completed and % grade.   I believe completed related to the minimum number of questions setting in the lesson.   The current lesson is made to be dependent upon only 1 other lesson.  Thus for example, #2 would be dependent upon #1, #3 dependent upon #2, #4 dependent upon #3: but a lesson can only be dependent upon 1 other lesson. There is an activity locking addin for 1.5.3  which is not part of the standard package.  It is similar to lesson dependency but deals with other types of activities.   My organization uses this in conjunction with Certificates.  Activity locking is my site administrator's responsibility in 1.5.3.  I am working in 1.6 and once the addin is ready for 1.6, then I will be playing with it  prior to it going live on our production server . Hope this helps a little.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: wrong answer default reply
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Bonnie, One can easily get bewildered by the quantity of parameters available in the Lesson settings. About the 'wild card' It only works with more recent versions of Moodle 1.5+ You have to be careful where you place it in your list of "teacher-answers". Consider the following scenario (tested in Moodle 1.5.3stable). the opposite of white is __________ Short Answer Answer 1: black Response 1: ok for black Score 1: 2 Jump 1: Next page Answer 2: gray Response 2: not quite! Score 2: 1 Jump 2: This page Answer 3: * Response 3: no way Score 3: 0 Jump 3: This page Answer 4: pink Response 4: why pink? Score 4: 0 Jump 4: This page If you switch the contents of Answer3 (& Response 3, etc.) with those of Answer 4, i.e. if you place the wild card asterisk at the end of your scenario, then, if the student types "pink", he will not get the Response "why pink?" but the response "no way". For the wild card to work it must be placed before any answer(s) having a null score . This is not logical, but that's the way it works. If you need a more advanced system of short answer analysis in the Lesson module, I recommend using the new Lesson module in Moodle 1.6(now in beta stage) and ticking the "use regular expressions" box. More info here . Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Using Lessons for a Tutorial
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello.  I am quite new to this.  I am trying to set up a tutorial for chemistry.  I merely want to give a question and, regardless of the answer given by the student, I would like to have the answer and it's explanation appear. Is there an easy way to do this?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Using Lessons for a Tutorial
ResponsesInList.Text: Easiest is to set all jumps to the next page.  In the next page put your content. This is what I call a foreshadow question. At least two other ways to do this. 1. In the incorrect answer's response to the question, you can point out the correct way. By the mistake, you can craft the way you respond, just like you do in class. 2a. Set the jump for one or more responses to a different page. On that page, maybe titled Answer to Question 1, put in your explaination. Then set the jump on that page to go back to either the question again, or the next page in the navigational order. 2b. Another way might be to tell the student in the response to their answer, what to look for, and have the jump send them back to page which deals with this question. This puts them back in navagational order and they will then review all the pages, including the question they missed. Hopefully they get it right the second time. I am sure there are other ways, like linking to a document, powerpoint etc. But this to me is the most straight forward. Does this help?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Lesson - high learning curve - improvement strategy
ResponsesInList.Text:
Bill, I first want to thank you for your comments. And I agree that once you leave the basics, it is a steep learning curve, where small steps don't seem to help a newbie navigate the tangle of clusters of branches. (that was good). I don't know if this helps, but here is what I do. In short, I deal with adults in a certified training environment which involves blended presentation of material. Moodle often serves as the pre req homework component of training that involves face to face time. This will not be a demonstration of applied innovative educational philosophy. The real short version: Our lessons are first created as a straight
line series of content pages with no jumps or question attached to
them. Thank goodness "next page" is the lesson default. Without putting too fine a point on it, the content is converted from talking head powerpoints. Then we insert questions every so often to loop the trainee back
in the logical order 5-8 slides for a mandatory review. No clusters, end of branches or even branch descriptions with jumps. That is the start. I view that as a story board. It is like a column of important numbers in a spreadsheet with no formulas. You look at each page or each number and decide if you want to do something different or better. My boss told me to use branch pages for the content pages. So I've gone back and changed some of them to question pages, and I have added more questions or content pages to the straight line presentation. Recently, I've started go back and be more creative in a page's content. Add an antimated graphic, put a link to a PDF file . We will be adding streaming video later. And I am thinking about some critical questions that a trainee gets wrong, how are our instructors going to add addition content pages to cover that miss and then get them back to that missed question again. And when our little flash files are ready, I be ready to change a miss question's jump to link there and know it will come back. Enlightnment is around the corner, trust me. Chris
