ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Using Quiz questions in Lesson
ResponsesInList.Text: Hey Martin and Moodlers, I have been pondering about how to switch Lesson to use the question classes for quite some time now. Although the process might seem rather straight forward, it is actually a very long and arduous journey. I believe that there are four top-level tasks: adding support for the question class, change the attempts logic, fix code breaks, and database migration. Each of these has several sub-tasks. Ill break these down best I can with the following: Adding support for the question class: This is one of the easier tasks. Just implement the question code and the interfaces for adding them to a Lesson. Printing the question(s) for attempts. Grading the question(s). Provide a method for adding new questions to a Lesson. When adding a question, display questions in course question bank to select from. Provide links/tabs for creating new questions, importing, etc. After adding a question, define possible jumps. Changing the attempts logic: Among other Lesson table changes, one that is the most significant is changing the lesson_attempts table. Instead of storing one attempt record per question answer, lesson_attempts should store one record per Lesson attempt. The functionality of the original lesson_attempts table will be replaced by the question_states table. Fixing code breaks: By switching to the question class, nearly all of the current Lesson code will be broken and must be replaced or fixed. Here is a quick breakdown of foreseeable code breaks along with relative difficulty in fixing the break: High scores (easy) Lesson statistics (hard - quiz reports might provide a jump start?) Essay Grading (medium - rewrite or migrate quiz's Manual Grading to the question code) Page Editing (easy) Jump type interpretation algorithms (medium) Ongoing score (easy) Progress bar (easy) Backup/restore (hard - rewrite for new table structures and add support for restoring Lessons pre question class support) Database migration: This will be a tremendous feat! Lesson tables need to be changed and their old data needs to be moved to new tables. Some of this code will be used in the restore process as well. Here is a basic overview of the upgrade process: migrate lesson_pages and lesson_answer content to question tables. migrate lesson_attempts to question_states. Re-organization of the lesson tables. Rebuild the Lesson. Side effects of this rewrite: Due to the amount of rewrites and modifications to the Lesson code, a couple side affects and opportunities arise:

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Using Quiz questions in Lesson
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Dan, You bring up a good point.  This migration would allow all of the question pages inside of a Lesson to behave just like Quiz's questions (be able to view/edit them in the course question bank and in other courses).  There are four other types of Lesson pages though: Branch Table, End of Branch, End of Cluster and Cluster.  The last three are not really pages at all.  The new Lesson database structure (which exists only in my head at the moment ) would take care of that.  But, branch tables are the one page that is not a question type but has a title, content, options and etc.  Now, there is a question type that is very close to branch tables called Description.  This question type could be modified to take the place of branch tables, or a new question type could be created.  A new feature of the question types is the display.html templates, which would be needed for displaying branch tables with slide show on or off. So, I guess the question is, would we want to get rid of Branch Tables all together as we know it?  Then replace it by expanding Description or by creating a new question type.  If branch tables are converted to a question type, then all Lesson pages would be stored in the course question bank and available to other courses or modules. Cheers, Mark

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scoring behaving oddly for numerical question
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Lane, Numerical question type is expecting a number (whole or decimal) and not fractions. So instead of 1/5, 1/4, 1/3, and 1/2 use .2, .25, .33, and .5 You can also specify ranges. For example, some users might enter .333 for 1/3. So you could do .33:.334 so that it accepts more numbers. If you want to continue to use fractions though, you can switch to Short answer and it will handle the fractions with no problem. Let me know if this works out for you, Mark

ResponsesInList.Title: Error opening and closing dates in Calendar

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Error opening and closing dates in Calendar
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Paul, What appears as a bug here is due to the way the Moodle calendar interprets the period of time during which a "lesson" is open as compared to current date. Example: Today is Nov. 6th Case 1 (normal behavior) in lesson settings, a lesson is set to be available from Nov. 7th until Nov. 10th In the calendar the only highlighted date is Nov. 7th, and dates 8th through 10th are "boxed" (i.e. they display a top and bottom border). In the calendar, if you click on Nov. 7th, it takes you to the calendar day view, where you can see the details of lesson opening and closing. Case 2 (the buggy situation) in lesson settings, a lesson is set to be available from Nov. 1st until Nov. 10th In the calendar the only highlighted date is Nov. 10th, in which we can see the double message you mention: Lesson opens; lesson closes... twice Obviously, Case2 should be considered as a bug since when a lesson's opening date is overdue we shoud not get the doubly double message in the due date box. What we should really see is a single message saying "lesson closes" that's all. I have posted bug report #4279 Joseph

ResponsesInList.Title: Bug #4174 - Lesson Essay Question Can't be Graded
ResponsesInList.Text:
I have entered this into the bug tracker... In the lesson module, a teacher will get the error "Error: could not
find grades" if they try to mark a lesson essay before the student has
completed the lesson. When the teacher goes to the lesson screen, they will see that there is
an essay to mark even if the student hasn't completed the lesson. If
they try to mark the essay, they will get that error. The problem stems
from the code trying to 'update' the grade record. Because the student
hasn't completed the rest of the lesson, the record doesn't exist yet,
and generates the error. To fix it, either the lesson should not allow the essay to be marked
until after the lesson has been completed, or it should create a grade
record if one doesn't exist. mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Bug #4174 - Lesson Essay Question Can't be Graded
ResponsesInList.Text:
Thanks for finding this. the lesson should not allow the essay to be marked
until after the lesson has been completed This would be the best solution.  Creating a grade record could potentially break several things.

ResponsesInList.Title: Lesson, Reloaded
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, we got a nice contract that involved making some changes to lesson. We reviewed them with Ray, and now they are in CVS for 1.5. The short list Custom scoring: answers can have a range of positive and negative values Ongoing score display: shows students a running total of their score Practice lessons: non graded lessons that don't show up in the gradebook Password protected lessons Short essay questions Random branch table within a standard path lesson (for creating simulations) Question clustering (set a series of questions from which one will be chosen randomly) Timed lessons. Lesson timer shows the time a student has left. Tree view: shows entire lesson as a list of links Slide show, allows you to set a custom page size and background color for a lesson Display left menu: shows a lesson menu on the left side of the screen ( requires new styles be added to the styles.php in your theme ). Display high scores: allows students to enter their name and high score if their score is one of the top number the lesson author has set. Set defaults: lesson settings can be saved as defaults for a course We're still working on getting the docs in the help files, but you can check out documentation here: http://learn.humboldt.edu/mod/book/view.php?id=619&chapterid=69 Let us know what you think . All the standard lesson settings still work so you can create lessons the usual way or mix and match the above options.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: sesskey - Lesson >> Reloaded
ResponsesInList.Text: You are wrong, sesskey is a security feature. IMO you should not add: $SESSION->sesskey = !empty($USER->id) ? $USER->sesskey : ''; insteand use $USER->sesskey in form Sesskey was introduced in Moodle 1.4.2. All third party code must be updated to send $USER->sesskey as a page parameter for pages that check its presence. What is sesskey? It is a random number unique for each user session, it is used to verify that page request comes from the user and not some embedded HTML code posted by evil cracker. All actions that change important data in database should be protected by sesskey. First insert sesskey as post or get parameter and then check it again on the target page (which processes the request) using confirm_sesskey(). Thats all. skodak

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Question Page - How to offer "Continue" vs actual Question
ResponsesInList.Text: Create a question, like multichoice, with a title and page content and without any answers and responses.  When you see the page in Check Navigation , it will have a Continue button at the bottom of the page.  This button will skip all feedback and jump to the next page. Note: make sure in your lesson settings that you set Action after correct answer: Normal - follow lesson path.  Otherwise your pages may shuffle. You can also accomplish all this by using branch tables.  Create a branch table, type in your title and content and one description.  For the description, type in Continue and then have the description jump to Next Page (or to Topic X, Page X). Have fun, Mark

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Embedding Audio
ResponsesInList.Text: <embed> and <object> tags are not allowed by default in text submitted by users - such as forum posts, glossary. If you do not mind lower security put in your config.php following: $CFG->allowobjectembed = true; Any tags including embed, object and script are allowed for teachers in activities such as Resouce, Book, Lesson. There is a bug in lesson module, instead of format_text($contents) it should use: $formatoptions->noclean = true; echo format_text($content, FORMAT_HTML, $formatoptions, $course->id); Noclean means that the text is by a trusted user (== teacher) and should be put on page without security filtering.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: flashcards in a part of a lesson
ResponsesInList.Text:
Flashcards would randomize the whole lesson.  In lesson 1.5 you can wrap questions in a Cluster page and an End of Cluster page to create randomization. So, set up your lesson as follows: Intro pages... Cluster Question Page 1 Question Page 2 Question Page ... End of Cluster End of the Lesson or More Pages This way the student sees the intro pages, then hits the cluster and all the question pages are random (or like flashcard).  Also, all questions within the cluster should jumpto "This page" or "
Unseen question within a cluster".  Do this if you want to hit all the questions in the cluster.

We want to keep it all within one lesson to simplify linking back to pages within the lesson from answers, as well as to simplify tracking. We also plan to implement this for a student view, to enable navigating long lessons non-linearly. Our next steps are to add custom scoring, so that different answers can have different scores (probably scoring on the click rather than on the jump)  a tree view for student navigation, and eventually variables that change the 'right' answer (in our project, some answers are 'right' at a low budget situation while others become more right as the budget improves). Basically this project long term involves building a scenario building/role playing/simulation module similar in many ways to Quandry & so far our clients like the start we've made with Lesson in Moodle. We're implementing these feature as selectable in the config area for the most part, but I realize this complicates the module a good deal beyond its original intentions. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: more questions about grading
ResponsesInList.Text: I have only used the lesson module for 1.5 but the answers may be helpful. On the lesson setup screen, you choose what percentage the lesson should be graded out of.  Typically I use 100%. For each individual question you select a number of points, this is to weigh the questions when calculating the total.  Then the number correct is divided by the total and the percent (out of the total possible percent you set earlier) is given. For the pages where you want text but no response, just a 'continue' you should use a branch table, this is basically a window where you enter text, and the student selects a button (one or several) that redirect him to a new page.  (i.e. continue -> next page, or four buttons go to page 1, go to page 2 etc..) Hope this was helpful.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Continuing with a lesson after timed out
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi James, if the timer runs out they are kind of stuck, they can restart the lesson if 'can retake' is set to yes, of course, or if you clear attempts, but this will start them on a fresh copy of the lesson, without their old responses. ResponsesInList.Text:
José, it has nothing to do with Moodle. It's a browser issue (again!). The proposed solution doesn't work with MSIE... only with Mozilla Browsers. The problem is the deprecated <embed> tag. It is no more in the HTML standard 4.01 and therefore there has been this workaround as described on the Macromedia website (object tag for MSIE, embed tag for Mozilla). MSIE seems to confuse this workaround (nesting embed tag in the object tag). I also noticed some problems when editing with MSIE. Here's another workaround: 
```text
<embed src="http://www.yourdomain.com/file.php/NN/imagenes/animaciones/m4-u1-acciones/m4-u1-acciones.swf" quality="high" pluginspage="http://www.macromedia.com/go/getflashplayer" type="application/x-shockwave-flash" width="232" height="334"></embed>
```
 I tested this with Mozilla Firefox 0.9.2, NS 7.1 and MSIE 6.0.2 and it worked. Maybe Opera, Safari, ...etc users can post if this works there, too. I will investigate if there is a (prefered) solution with the object tag, too. This would be better since the object tag is HTML 4.01 standard. Andreas

Finally, I'm not sure I understand the idea behind the clusters, could I ask you to provide a little example? Clusters appear as a single question page to the navigation system, but when you link to a cluster, a page within the cluster is chosen at random. This makes it easy to make variations of your questions so that students get a different question each time they take the lesson. This also makes it pretty frustrating for students to try and cheat (esp in a random unseen page lesson, which will choose clusters at random order). So you add a cluster, put some questions in the cluster, and then add an end of cluster. Link a page to the cluster, and it will choose a question at random, then go where that question tells it to depending on the answer.

Anyway, they are originally just for make a list of contents, but many folks use them like slides to place instructional content. Are you clicking the 'check navigation' button after you create a page? If so, this sends you into a place where you can navigate the lesson like a student, and so you can't edit it there. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: It was pretty hard
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Martin, most of our changes are optional. The left menu in fact also requires custom styles added to the theme. Its funny how things look, to me the unique thing about lesson was being able to build multiple branchs . We use this (along with inter-branch randomization code) to build simulations. You could use our code to built a learning object something like Myst, for instance. Or a simple series of questions. Or a slide show style presentation with embedded questions, with a left navigation menu for non-linear access. The questions might be clustered so the student gets a different set each time, or not. So one use scenario is you want to have students discuss a subject, but you want them to have a certain level of knowledge about the subject first. So you put readings or pictures or audio or video or a mix into a presentation, and you put some questions in every few pages of the presentation. You give them a quiz grade for incentive & you tell them to do that before entering the discussion. So now you have a way to know if the students experienced the material, some idea of what level of knowledge a student making a discussion post has of the material, etc. This was all funded by a group who basically put their textbook online (along with new video and audio files), and now the 'self-assessment' questions that were static in the text are integrated into the online version.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: copying a lesson to another class
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Matt Click the Backup link in Settings block on your course homepage. Select "Yes" for all of the activities in your course you want to include in your backup (in your case just lessons) and select "None" in the users field. Click continue, and then continue, then continue again. You will be taken to the files area on your course, where you will see your backed up course stored as a zip file. Right click on your backed up course to save it to your computer. Next create a new moodle course(s) (or if you don't have rights to do so, ask your moodle administrator), then upload the zip file to the files area in the new course. You can then click Restore and follow the instrutions that follow to load the lesson into the new course(s). Morag

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Importing Lessons

ResponsesInList.Title: Grading, chaining and perfection
ResponsesInList.Text: 1. Grading There are a lot of applications of grading in a module as Lesson. I use grading to let the student have a parameter to know, at once, how good is his learning, instead of waiting to make next quiz, and I suggest everybody not to avoid to do the same. In the last page of the lesson, I usually write: at the next click you will be graded, if grading is equal or better than xxx go on with other activities , if is worse than xxx I suggest you to repeat the lesson (or to ask for help by the teacher). After that, the student goes to a new page where he finds some congratulations (hoping that he has not got a grading like 1 of 100...) and the grading. I'm certain he remembers yet which was the threshold (with the actual method of grading I have to change the threshold level at each lesson), but you never know... It would be better (of course, if possible) that a teacher would have two fields, within the lesson settings, where to write a code (short name) of the lesson and the grading threshold. So, in the grading page, the student could read either: "Your grading is yyy, that is equal or more than the sufficiency level that was xxx, so you have passed this lesson and you may go to the next activity"; or: "Your grading is zzz, that less than the sufficiency level that was xxx, so we suggest you to repeat the lesson or to ask for help by the teacher".
